The theme here seems to be the persistence of a problem related to education or upbringing.

This might be a metaphor for the pursuit of knowledge being unattainable or the idea that those who seek knowledge (fayz, which can mean divine grace or enlightenment) can't access earthly things. The theme here is the separation between the seeker of knowledge and the material world, or the futility of trying to get earthly things while seeking higher knowledge.

It's saying that even a particle of upbringing learned the work of the sun, and to the moth of piety, the power of Solomon was given. This seems to be about how even small elements of education or virtue can lead to great achievements. The sun's work (light, warmth) and Solomon's power (wisdom, strength) are given to those with a particle of upbringing or piety. So the theme is the transformative power of education or piety, leading to significant gains.

The theme here is the value of perseverance or the transformation of small efforts into something significant.
